definition: The BigScience Large Open-science Open-access Multilingual Language Model (BLOOM) is an open-access large language model (LLM) released in 2022.
details: It was created by a volunteer-driven research effort to provide a transparently-created alternative to proprietary AI models. With 176 billion parameters, BLOOM is a transformer-based autoregressive model designed to generate text in 46 natural languages and 13 programming languages. The model is distributed under the project's "Responsible AI License".

explainer.lead: BLOOM is a 176-billion-parameter language model released in 2022 that generates text in 46 natural languages and 13 programming languages. It matters because BigScience made it open access through a volunteer-driven effort, offering a transparently created alternative to proprietary models.

tiers.eli5: BLOOM is like a very large autocomplete that has learned how words and code usually continue. You give it a beginning, and it keeps adding the next piece until it forms an answer. A big group of volunteers made it openly available so more people could study and use it.
tiers.practitioner: Use BLOOM by supplying a prompt and decoding its output autoregressively, with each generated token fed back into the model. It can be applied to text in its 46 supported natural languages or code in its 13 supported programming languages. Check the Responsible AI License for usage conditions, and treat generated text or code as output to review rather than guaranteed-correct content.
tiers.paperLevel: BLOOM is a transformer-based autoregressive language model with 176 billion parameters, modeling a token sequence as p(x) = product_t p(x_t | x_<t). It was created by the BigScience research effort and released in 2022 for 46 natural languages and 13 programming languages. Its autoregressive text-generation formulation does not itself guarantee factual correctness or executable code.

explainer.example: Given the prompt "Write a function that adds two numbers," BLOOM can generate a continuation containing a function in one of its supported programming languages, adding one token at a time.

flow: Start with a text or code prompt.
The transformer processes the prompt using its learned parameters.
The model predicts and adds a next token.
The new token becomes part of the input.
Repeat until the desired continuation is generated.
explainer.origin: BLOOM was created by BigScience, a volunteer-driven research effort, and released in 2022. Its purpose was to provide a transparently created, open-access alternative to proprietary AI models.
explainer.lineage: BLOOM belongs to the family of large transformer-based autoregressive language models. Its full name is BigScience Large Open-science Open-access Multilingual Language Model.
explainer.whyItMatters: BLOOM combines broad multilingual and programming-language coverage with open access. Its volunteer-driven creation also demonstrates a transparent alternative to developing large language models behind proprietary boundaries.
